As a resident of Alaska who has lived in an off grid log cabin for 19 years I can give some advice. Of course it will require you to spend some money to get the things you need. If you have enough money to get a quality diesel generator around 8 KW this is a great way to go

. A water cooled unit runs in the neighborhood of 10K. Personally I have used a honda 2000 eu portable or the yamaha 2000 version. Both run about a $1000 each and come with a real 3 year warranty that includes full repair at any honda/yamaha service center.

Another important piece is to buy a propane fridge/ freezer - again over $1000 dollars but will cool down within 24 hours and allow you to use you generator for other power needs.

In California I would seriously consider solar power with a inverter / battery bank set up. I use one up here and it really helps in the summer but winter it is a non factor. In cali it should help year round. I run 10 solar panels as a supplement and would advise around 20 or more panels for a more serious set up. You can run the panels to the batteries for power and set up a 8KW diesel generator to run for 1 hour every time the batteries get low. Right off the bat that setup would decrease your generator run time down from 24 hours to 12. Add in solar power during day time and you might only have the generator run a couple hours every night saving you money and wear and tear on the generator.

Search the web for companies in california that sell off grid power setups. At the very least get yourself a little Honda or yamaha 2000 watt portable genny. They are super quiet and you can put 1000's of hours on them as long as you change the oil regularly before they need service.
